note: CODE DERIVATION: data/adamczyk_2022_ras.py melts the val2 .sav columns CESD1t1..CESD20t1 and strips the 't1' suffix (number-preserving rename; the deposit's typo 'CSED16t1' is renamed to CESD16t1 at load). The .sav carries NO item wording: variable labels are the bare column names ('CESD1t1'..) and there are no value labels, both levels checked for all 20 columns. The deposit's materials .docx (and the identical ESM supplement of the Sci Rep paper) only describes the scale -- 'Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression Scale (CES-D; Radloff, 1977) (Polish adaptation - Kaniasty, 2003) ... 20 statements ... past week ... four-point scale (0 = rarely, or not at all to 3 = most of the time or all the time)' -- and prints no item. The Polish Kaniasty (2003) wording is in a Gdansk book, outside the deposit and the paper's supplements. So mapping_basis=reconstructed: item_text is Radloff's English CES-D aligned to codes by reading CESD<i> as canonical item <i>; text_source=translated_substitute with language=Polish and no _translated columns (the 2026-09-01 fallback). translation_source=third_party_english: the stems are PMC11515990 Table 1 verbatim with its leading '1. ' numbering stripped, which states they are Radloff's; it diverges from Radloff 1977 in item 19 ('people dislike me', Radloff 'disliked') and item 20 (no quotation marks around 'going'). Instructions and the four anchors are PMC7543651's Appendix verbatim (its anchor list capitalises only the first). The study's own endpoint anchors ('rarely, or not at all' / 'most of the time or all the time') are consistent with these but were not shipped because the middle two are unpublished. STORAGE DIRECTION (checked, not assumed): the positively worded items 4/8/12/16 are stored ALREADY REVERSED -- all 20 item-rest correlations are positive (+0.27..+0.81; items 4/8/12/16 = +0.73/+0.52/+0.61/+0.69, where a raw positive CES-D item correlates negatively), and the depositors' own 'Depression' column equals the per-person mean of the 20 stored items for 209/209 respondents (9/209 if 4/8/12/16 are re-reversed). So for CESD4, CESD8, CESD12 and CESD16 the anchors ship DESCENDING (resp 0 = 'most or all of the time (5-7 days)', resp 3 = 'Rarely or none of the time'), ascending for the other 16 -- the same handling as conner_2017_cesd. RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register.csv row 'CES-D' verdict ship_with_note (Ben 2026-09-23, irw#2381 R06) applied, not re-derived. Quoted clause: 'This scale is free to use without permission' (CamCOPS, camcops.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tasks/cesd.html, quoting the CES-D Stanford Version PDF). Caveat the register requires stating: that evidence is secondhand; the originator is NIMH (Radloff, federal work) and no restriction was found anywhere, which is why it ships. The Polish adaptation's own terms are moot: IRW ships the English original, not Kaniasty's wording. Deposit CC BY 4.0. Step 3b: the 20 CESD columns sit in the val2 file beside MHC-SF, SELSA, RAS and SF-12 blocks and reconstruct the file's own 'Depression' score exactly, so the table is the CES-D and not a sibling measure. Per-item n = 209 for every item.
public_note: Respondents answered the Polish CES-D adaptation (Kaniasty, 2003), but neither the deposit nor the paper publishes the Polish wording, so the item text is Radloff's (1977) English CES-D; the positively worded items CESD4, CESD8, CESD12 and CESD16 are stored already reverse-scored (the depositors' own depression score is the mean of the stored values), so their anchors run from 'most or all of the time' at 0 to 'rarely or none of the time' at 3.
